articleSummary: As of 12 March 2026, Nipah virus remains a regional threat across South Asia and Southeast Asia, with recurrent outbreaks since the 1999 Malaysia origin, high mortality, and frequent hospital transmission. Reservoirs are fruit bats; spillover occurs when bats contaminate food or surfaces, with pigs acting as amplifying hosts in some settings. Ecological and social changes—deforestation, urban expansion, agricultural intensification—increase human–bat contact and spillover risk. Cross-border movement and informal animal trade raise regional spillover risk to Cambodia, Thailand, and the Philippines. Health systems, especially rural facilities, often lack diagnostics, PPE, and trained personnel, risking nosocomial amplification and limited laboratory capacity. A continuous One Health approach with stable funding, surveillance, ecological monitoring, cross-border communication, and accelerated development of vaccines and therapeutics is essential to prevent escalation.

articleHeadline: Chạy đua giành lại sự sống cho các bệnh nhi ngộ độc botulinum
articleSummary: Five members of a Da Nang family developed suspected botulism after eating fermented fish on March 9. Three children (ages 7, 11, 15) were severely ill; one child on dialysis could not be transferred, while two siblings were moved to Da Nang's Hospital for Women and Children for intensive care. Initially, one patient required ventilation and others showed respiratory distress. Botulism Antitoxin Heptavalent (BAT) is scarce in Vietnam, priced at about $8,000 per vial. To treat the crisis, WHO arranged an emergency supply of five BAT vials transported from Switzerland via Geneva → Istanbul → Hanoi to Da Nang. Administration occurred overnight March 11 and finished around 02:00 on March 12. By morning March 12, two treated children were alert, responsive, and able to move limbs, though ventilation continued. Authorities call for domestic BAT stockpiling and reinforced food-safety surveillance of fermented foods.

articleHeadline: WHO rushes botulism antitoxin to Vietnam for 3 poisoned children
articleSummary: Five vials of Botulism Antitoxin Heptavalent (BAT) are being shipped from Switzerland to Vietnam to treat three Vietnamese children suspected of botulinum poisoning after eating fermented fish. WHO’s Vietnam representative Angela Pratt said the emergency supply aims to reach patients quickly. The shipment will arrive at Noi Bai International Airport in Hanoi, with Da Nang health authorities collecting the medicine and transporting it to the city for treatment. Earlier this week, a Da Nang hospital treated five patients for suspected food poisoning from fermented fish; one patient tested positive for Clostridium botulinum, while the three children are reported in serious condition. BAT costs about US$8,000 per vial and is rarely stocked. Vietnam has had only a small number of botulism cases recently; WHO has previously shipped emergency antitoxin to Vietnam in 2020 and 2023.
notes: ベトナムでは過去にもボツリヌス症例があり（2020年、2023年にもWHOからの抗毒素輸送実績）、完全に異常な事例ではない。発酵魚製品が原因と特定されており、食品安全の問題。抗毒素1バイアルあたり約8,000ドルと高額で在庫が少ない特殊医薬品であることから、WHOを通じた国際的な緊急支援が必要とされている。患者5名中1名でClostridium botulinum陽性が確認されており、診断は確定的。小児3名が重篤であることから重症度は高いが、ヒト-ヒト感染はなく、食品媒介性の限定的な事例と考えられる。

articleSummary: Taiwan's CDC reports 2025 syphilis cases totaling 9,935 nationwide, up from 9,737 in 2024; among ages 15–24, new syphilis cases rose to 1,892 from 1,754 (+8%). articleSummary: As of early March 2026, Korea reports about 20 African swine fever (ASF) outbreaks this year. FAO’s Asia-Pacific ASF update (Feb 2026) notes ASF has spread to more than 20 countries, including Korea, North Korea, Vietnam, and the Philippines. In Korea, a virus detected in November 2025 in Dangjin, Chungnam, was identified as IGR-I rather than IGR-II, suggesting introduction via humans or contaminated goods. Wild boar detections continue across Gangwon and Gyeonggi, with Hwacheon accounting for 509 cumulative detections. Domestic plasma protein contamination debates persist as authorities test samples. Vaccine progress: Komipharm reports 100% survival in three-shot trials in the Philippines; Korea’s Central Vaccine Research Institute advances an MEC-01–based candidate (ASF-X) with trials in Vietnam and the Philippines and a 2027 global release target.

articleSummary: Three-year-old Russian girl vacationing in Bali developed a severe bacterial skin infection after a mosquito bite followed by a warm pool swim. She received antihistamines and topical ointments and was prohibited from swimming in the sea or pool until full recovery. The SHOT report highlights travel-related pediatric impetigo risk linked to insect bites, skin trauma, and contaminated water in tropical tourist destinations such as Bali, Indonesia. articleSummary: Leptospirosis cases are rising across the state, including Bengaluru, with over 16,000 cases and about 30 deaths reported in the past five years. By 2025, 6,525 cases were recorded and 19 deaths occurred that year. Leptospirosis is a zoonotic bacterial infection spread through urine-contaminated water or soil. Initial symptoms often mimic dengue or malaria and appear 2–14 days after exposure. Mild symptoms include fever, severe headache, body aches (especially legs and back), chills, vomiting, red eyes, weakness, and abdominal pain; severe disease can involve kidney failure, jaundice, respiratory problems, meningitis, and internal bleeding. Prevention stresses avoiding contact with contaminated water, wearing boots and gloves during farming or waste disposal, washing after exposure, covering wounds, sanitation, rodent control, and drinking clean water. Laboratory confirmation starts with IgM ELISA; MAT is the main confirmatory test in specialized labs, with PCR for early detection. Delayed treatment can be life-threatening.
notes: カルナータカ州・ベンガルール地域における複数疾患（レプトスピラ症、デング、マラリア）の同時流行の可能性。レプトスピラ症の症例数が過去5年間で継続的に増加しており、2025年単年で6,525件・19名死亡は公衆衛生上の重大な懸念。汚染水・土壌への曝露が原因で、農業従事者・廃棄物処理作業者など職業曝露リスクが高い。初期症状がデング・マラリアと類似しており診断遅延のリスクあり。腎不全・黄疸・呼吸障害など重症化リスクも存在。齧歯類対策・衛生管理の強化が必要。国際的拡大リスクは現時点で不明だが、地域的な流行規模と重症度から継続監視が必要。

articleSummary: A man in his 30s in China developed seizures after six months of consuming raw pig blood, highlighting neurocysticercosis as a serious risk. Neurocysticercosis accounts for 60–80% of cysticercosis cases in China, with about 3 million infections nationwide. In July 2025, the Shanwei, Guangdong resident had sudden limb convulsions and loss of consciousness for ~2 minutes. Initial MRI revealed an intracranial lesion; tumors were considered but later excluded after Guangzhou evaluations. A right frontal lobe lesion was suspected to be infectious. He then presented to Shulan (Hangzhou) Hospital, Infectious Diseases, where Dr. Gao Hainü and team synthesized past history, dietary exposure, and imaging to diagnose neurocysticercosis. articleHeadline: An ancient infection breaks out of Asia's fever zone
articleSummary: Scrub typhus, caused by Orientia, is breaking out of Asia's Tsutsugamushi Triangle with reports from Kenya, Senegal, South Africa, Cameroon and Djibouti indicating local circulation rather than imported infection. Kenyan serosurveys show measurable antibody positivity among febrile patients; Senegalese studies detect Orientia 16S rRNA in Mus musculus near the Senegal River; South Africa reports Orientia-like genetic signatures in domestic dogs suggesting potential novel strains; earlier Cameroon and Djibouti-linked illnesses implicate Candidatus Orientia chuto outside Asia. No confirmed chigger mite vector has been identified in Africa, contrasting with Asia where rodents, vectors and seasonality are well characterized. In India and broader Asia-Pacific, scrub typhus is seasonal with monsoon/post-monsoon waves; early doxycycline treatment saves lives; testing often follows malaria/dengue negativity. Implications include misdiagnosis risk, climate- and land-use changes in vectors, antimicrobial stewardship, and One Health surveillance to map vectors, reservoirs and human cases.
notes: 【重要所見】①つつが虫病の伝統的流行域（Tsutsugamushi Triangle）外への拡大：ケニア・セネガル・南アフリカ・カメルーン・ジブチで輸入例でなく地域循環を示唆。②アフリカでのベクター未同定：アジアと異なりツツガムシ媒介昆虫が確認されておらず伝播経路不明。③誤診リスク：マラリア・デングとの鑑別困難で見逃しの恐れ。④気候変動・土地利用変化がベクター分布変化に関与の可能性。⑤One Health監視体制構築の必要性。早期ドキシサイクリン治療が有効だが診断遅延が致命的。Novel Orientia株（Candidatus Orientia chuto）の出現も懸念材料。

articleHeadline: Could vaccine-carrying mosquitoes slow the spread of deadly diseases?
articleSummary: Experiments described in Nature.com used vaccine-carrying mosquitoes to curb transmission of rabies and Nipah virus from bats. Nipah has about 75% fatality in humans, while rabies approaches 100% fatality. In China, researchers fed mosquitoes vaccinated blood, triggering replication of the vaccine to the insects’ saliva glands; when these mosquitoes fed bats, bats developed antibodies against rabies and survived later exposure. Parallel tests with mice and hamsters bitten by the vaccinated insects showed similar antibody responses and protection. Danielle Anderson of the University of Melbourne cautioned that the results demonstrate vaccination potential for animals not yet exposed, but many bats already carry Nipah, and it remains unclear whether vaccinating bats would halt spread. Lead researcher Zhang said the work has limitations and is investigating whether the approach could prevent transfer from bats to livestock such as pigs. Scaling this to humans raises ethical concerns and practicality questions.

TB is an infectious, airborne disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (the Koch bacillus), primarily affecting the lungs but may involve other organs. Transmission occurs via cough, speech, or sneeze. Symptoms include a persistent cough longer than three weeks, afternoon fever, night sweats, fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite. Those with symptoms should seek a health unit for evaluation and a sputum exam to confirm the diagnosis; treatment is provided free by the Unified Health System (SUS). In Sorocaba, campaigns cover primary care units, ERs, and municipal centers; Itapetininga runs 'Fique Sabendo Tuberculose' with free testing and tents in busy areas, plus active case finding by Vigilância Epidemiológica. World TB Day on March 24 emphasizes early diagnosis and six months of continuous treatment to cure and prevent transmission.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Public health alert due to the spread of a fungus transmitted by cats
articleHeadline: Alerta sanitaria por la expansión de un hongo transmitido por gatos
articleSummary: Detected Sporothrix brasiliensis in Maldonado and Rocha, Uruguay—the first record in the country—raising regional public health concern. The Brazil-origin fungus transmits mainly through contact with infected cats and poses high risk of human infection; WHO notes zoonotic Sporothrix infections with over 11,000 human cases in the last decade across South America. Transmission occurs via scratches, bites, or contact with secretions and wounds of diseased animals. The first Uruguayan case followed a family that adopted a puppy from southern Brazil; infected cats show non-healing ulcers, crusts, hair loss, and conjunctivitis. In humans, nodules can evolve into ulcers and spread along lymphatics, potentially involving lungs, bones, or the nervous system, with meningitis or arthritis in severe cases. Protective gear is advised when handling sick animals; stray cat control remains challenging. Treatments with itraconazole or terbinafine require prolonged courses; regional labs enhance microscopy/culture-based diagnosis and authorities coordinate surveillance and veterinary collaboration.
notes: ウルグアイで国内初検出。ブラジル由来の真菌による人獣共通感染症で、主に感染猫との接触により伝播。過去10年間で南米全体で11,000人以上の症例が報告されており、WHOも注視。重症例では髄膜炎や関節炎に至る可能性。野良猫の管理が困難で継続的曝露リスクが高い。長期の抗真菌薬治療が必要。地域ラボでの診断体制強化と当局による監視・獣医連携が進行中。国境を越えた拡大（ブラジル→ウルグアイ）が既に発生しており、地域的な公衆衛生上の懸念となっている。

articleHeadline: El peligroso hongo que "transmiten los gatos" ya infectó a más de 11.000 personas en este país de Latinoamérica
articleSummary: Sporothrix brasiliensis, a zoonotic fungus transmitted from cats, originated in Brazil and has raised alarms across Uruguay and much of South America. The Uruguayan Institute of Hygiene confirmed cases in Maldonado and Rocha, signaling a shift in the regional epidemiology and prompting reinforced surveillance. The World Health Organization notes that in South American areas affected by this species—primarily Brazil—more than 11,000 human cases have been reported in the past decade. Transmission occurs through direct contact with infected cats, especially strays or animals with visible lesions. In felines, facial, muzzle, and paw ulcers are common and lesions with crusts facilitate transmission via scratches or bites to humans. In people, infections begin as skin and subcutaneous nodules, often along lymphatic channels; most are cutaneous but lymph nodes can be involved, requiring prolonged therapy. Early medical evaluation improves prognosis. Sporothrix brasiliensis is thermally dimorphic: filamentous at 25°C and yeast-like at 37°C.

articleSummary: As of 13 March 2026, a Vietnamese clinician from the Ho Chi Minh City University of Medicine and Pharmacy Hospital warns that botulism poisoning results from Clostridium botulinum in foods improperly processed or preserved. The bacteria thrive in anaerobic, sealed or naturally fermented environments. Common sources include fermented fish, salted or cured fish, other fermented meats, homemade canned foods, pâté, sausages, smoked meats, and pickled vegetables produced without hygiene. Ingestion of botulinum toxin can cause severe neurologic illness, starting with facial weakness, progressing to limb paralysis and possibly respiratory failure; death may occur without prompt treatment. Prevention focuses on safe preparation and storage: correct salt concentrations and fermentation times, discard bulging or foul-smelling cans, and ensure thorough cooking of homemade preserved items to inactivate toxin. Antitoxin therapy exists but is scarce and often imported from WHO or centers in Vietnam.

articleHeadline: How close is lumpy skin disease? New modelling signals weakest biosecurity points
articleSummary: LSDV poses no confirmed cases in Australia, but modelling maps two gateways: Port Hedland–Dampier in Western Australia and the northern Cape York Peninsula. Infected insects could reach via winds from Indonesia or by ships between WA and Southeast Asia. Windborne entry could occur hundreds of kilometres offshore; shipping routes add another pathway. LSD has spread in Asia, reaching Indonesia in 2022, bringing risk to Australia's north coast. Surveillance includes insect trapping, testing, and routine cattle monitoring. A confirmed incursion could trigger trade restrictions on live cattle, beef, and dairy exports. Led by Professor Ricardo Soares Magalhaes (University of Queensland), the model targets prioritized surveillance and is adaptable; published in Scientific Reports.
notes: 現時点で実際の発生ではなく、リスクモデリング研究の結果報告。LSDVはインドネシア（2022年）から風媒介昆虫や船舶経由でオーストラリア北部への侵入リスクがある。動物疾患であり人への直接的健康影響はないが、畜産業への経済的影響は重大。サーベイランス体制は整備されており、実際の侵入確認時には即座にPICKUPに格上げすべき事案。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Preventive surveillance actions for avian influenza continue in the southern part of the state - Jornal O Sul
articleHeadline: Prosseguem as ações de monitoramento preventivo da gripe aviária no Sul do Estado - Jornal O Sul
articleSummary: Preventive avian influenza surveillance continues in southern Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. By March 12, the Department of Vigilance and Animal Health Defense (DDA) within Seapi had trained 186 agents and held meetings with municipal authorities in Chuí, Rio Grande, and Santa Vitória do Palmar. The effort followed the first wild-bird case in late February at the Taim Ecological Reserve, with 23 birds (Coscoroba swans and mourning herons) testing positive. The SVO-RS reports permanent field presence and coordinated actions to end the outbreak. Suspected cases—birds with respiratory or neurological symptoms or sudden high mortality—must be reported immediately. Measures include a 10-km sanitary sweep around the focus, inspections of 93 subsistence poultry properties, and checks at commercial farms in Pelotas and ornamental-bird breeders in Santa Vitória do Palmar. Samples go to LFDA Campinas (OMSA reference) for confirmation, with Lagoa da Mangueira area under integrated operations with Mapa and ICMBio.
notes: ブラジル・リオグランデドスル州南部での野鳥（コスコローバ白鳥、サギ類23羽）における鳥インフルエンザ陽性例に対する予防的監視活動。186名の監視員訓練、10km圏内の衛生調査、93の家禽飼育施設の検査など組織的対応が実施されている。ヒト感染例の報告はなく、現時点では動物衛生上の問題。OMSAリファレンスラボでの確定検査実施中。家禽への拡大やヒト感染事例が発生した場合は再評価が必要。
